notes: Styling system: one hand-written stylesheet (styles.css) with CSS custom properties in :root and a prefers-color-scheme: dark override; no component library, no build step. Five static HTML pages (index, tool, basket, confirm, done) share app.js, which renders cards, calendar, listbox, basket, sessions and the confirm/done summaries as HTML strings. Token names differ from DESIGN.md roles (--color-ground = surface, --color-surface = surface-container, --color-accent = primary, --color-ok = success, --color-accent-tint = selection). Packet lint.json and census.json were empty ({} / []), so drift was found by reading styles.css and the inline styles directly. Bash was unavailable, so uie lint was not re-run. No builder notes were read. Line numbers are cited in evidence for the fixer only; they are not part of identity.

passes.summary: Read styles.css, app.js and the five HTML pages; checked tokens, states, keyboard models, forms, layout and motion.

out_of_scope: IME (en-GB only, no keydown handlers on text inputs)

not_assessable: uie lint was not re-run (Bash denied); packet lint.json and census.json were empty.
Rendered effects (overflow width at 320 px, truncation, contrast) are computed from the code and need verifier confirmation in the captures.

strengths.title: Global :focus-visible ring (3 px, --color-focus, offset 2 px) in both themes, and no outline: none anywhere
Motion is limited to background-color and opacity at the 120 ms token, with a prefers-reduced-motion path that removes both
Confirm form ties errors to fields (aria-invalid, aria-describedby) and focuses a role=alert error summary with links to each field; name and phone carry autocomplete
strengths.evidence: confirm.html fields; app.js initConfirm submit handler

strengths.title: Every interactive control has a 44 px minimum height, and Remove buttons carry the tool name in sr-only text
strengths.evidence: styles.css min-height: 44px on inputs, buttons, nav links, options; app.js basket render

candidates.title: Results grid minimum column of 330 px is wider than the content box at 320 px
candidates.description: Content must reflow without horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS px. The results grid uses repeat(auto-fill, minmax(330px, 1fr)); at a 320 px viewport the page has 16 px padding each side, leaving a 288 px content box, so the single column is 330 px and overflows by about 42 px.
candidates.impact: Phone members on small screens may get a horizontally scrolling page with the right edge of every tool card, including its badge, cut off.

evidence.detail: minmax(330px,1fr) inside .page padding var(--space-4) both sides; 320 - 32 = 288 < 330

factor_notes.frequency: Every visit to the find page at widths below 362 px.

candidates.recommendation: Use minmax(min(100%, 330px), 1fr) or a smaller minimum.

candidates.title: Tool names on cards are cut to one line, hiding the words that tell similar tools apart
candidates.description: A name that identifies the item should be readable in full. .card__name a sets white-space: nowrap with text-overflow: ellipsis. Beside a 96 px thumbnail, a 375 px card leaves about 200 px for 17 px bold text, so 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' and '... one battery' both truncate before the distinguishing words, and 'Manual tile cutter, 600 mm' vs 'Electric wet tile saw, 180 mm' lose their size. No title attribute or other full-name exposure is provided.
candidates.impact: Members comparing tools on a phone may open the wrong drill or need to open each card to tell them apart.

locations.snippet: white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis

evidence.detail: single-line ellipsis on the card link; two drill names differ only after the 27th character

factor_notes.frequency: Every card on phone widths; worst for the two drills.

candidates.recommendation: Let the name wrap (or clamp to two or three lines) and keep the padded touch target.

candidates.title: Search with no matches leaves the previous results and count on screen
candidates.description: A search must show its outcome, including an empty result. search() calls render() and updates the status only when list.length is non-zero; with zero matches it returns silently, so the earlier result list (on first search, all ten tools) remains and the live status is not updated. There is no empty-state markup.
candidates.impact: A member searching for a tool the library does not hold may believe the unrelated tools shown are matches, and screen-reader users hear nothing.

evidence.detail: no else branch; results and #results-status untouched when TOOLS.filter(matches) is empty

factor_notes.frequency: Any search or filter combination with no match (e.g. 'saw' + Garden, or a late date).

candidates.recommendation: Always render; on zero matches show an empty state naming the query with a way to clear filters, and set the status to 'No tools found'.

candidates.title: Loan-length listbox captures Tab and has no Escape or outside-click close
candidates.description: A listbox popup should close on Escape and let Tab move focus onward. The keydown handler on #loan-list calls preventDefault on Tab and moves to the next option (wrapping), so Tab and Shift+Tab never leave the open list; Escape is not handled; clicking elsewhere does not close it. The only exits are choosing an option (Enter, Space, click) or re-clicking the button.
candidates.impact: Keyboard users who open the list to check the options may be unable to Tab out without changing their choice, and are not told how to leave.

evidence.detail: Tab preventDefault + focus next option; no Escape branch; no focusout/document click handler

factor_notes.frequency: Each time a keyboard user opens the loan list.
factor_notes.impact: Focus held in the popup; Escape does nothing.

candidates.recommendation: Let Tab close the list and continue; add Escape to close and return focus to the button; close on focusout. A native select (two options) would remove the custom model.

candidates.title: Continue and Confirm show no visible pending state during their 1.2 s and 1.5 s waits
candidates.description: An action that takes more than about a second should show it is in progress. On submit, #continue and #confirm only receive aria-busy="true"; styles.css has no [aria-busy] or loading style, the label does not change and the buttons are not disabled, so nothing on screen changes for 1.2 s (basket) and 1.5 s (confirm).
candidates.impact: Members on a phone may think the tap did not register and tap again or leave.

evidence.detail: setTimeout 1200 / 1500 ms with no visual change

factor_notes.impact: No feedback for over a second.

candidates.recommendation: Style .button[aria-busy=true] (spinner or 'Confirming…' label) in the shared button component and ignore repeat submits while busy.

candidates.title: Submitting the confirm form twice allocates two reservation numbers
candidates.description: A repeated submit must not create a second reservation. The confirm submit handler pushes a new reference (FT-4471 + count) into sessionStorage before its 1.5 s wait and does not guard against re-entry; the button stays enabled. A second tap within the wait pushes FT-4472 for the same items and slot, and done.html then lists 'Reservation numbers FT-4471 and FT-4472'.
candidates.impact: Members who tap twice may be shown two reservation numbers for one tool and be unsure which is real, or the desk may hold the tool twice.

evidence.detail: no in-flight flag; ref allocated per submit; done page joins all refs for the slot with ' and '

factor_notes.frequency: Whenever a member taps Confirm again during the silent 1.5 s wait.

candidates.recommendation: Set an in-flight flag (or disable via aria-disabled) on first submit and allocate the reference once.

candidates.title: Expired hold shows 'Something went wrong. Try again.' and every retry fails the same way
candidates.description: An error should say what happened and offer a way out. When the 10-minute hold has passed, the basket submit shows the generic message 'Something went wrong. Try again.' Nothing resets hold_started, so holdExpired() stays true and every retry fails identically; the hold length is never shown to the member beforehand.
candidates.impact: A member who took more than ten minutes, perhaps comparing tools in the evening, may be stuck on the basket with no way to finish and no explanation.

evidence.detail: HOLD_MINUTES = 10; hold_started only cleared by 'Reserve another tool' on done.html

factor_notes.frequency: Any session longer than ten minutes from first add.
factor_notes.impact: Dead end; task cannot be completed without clearing storage or the done page.

candidates.recommendation: Explain that the hold ran out, re-check availability and restart the hold (or let the member extend it); state the hold length up front.

candidates.title: Closed days can be chosen as pick-up days and are rejected only at the final confirm
candidates.description: Invalid choices should be prevented or flagged where they are made. The tool calendar renders all 21 days as enabled buttons; only open days carry an 'Open' tag. The closed-day check runs only after Confirm reservation (after a 1.5 s wait), and its error item is plain text with no link back to the tool page to change the day.
candidates.impact: Members may pick a closed day, fill in their details and only then learn the day is not possible, with no direct route back to change it.

locations.snippet: so this pick-up day is not possible. Choose another day.

evidence.detail: no isOpenDay check at selection or Reserve; check at confirm only; error <li> has no link

factor_notes.frequency: 15 of the 21 calendar days are closed.
factor_notes.persistence: Every time a closed day is chosen.

candidates.recommendation: Make closed days non-selectable (aria-disabled with a reason) or validate at Reserve; link any late error to the tool page with the day pre-filled.

candidates.title: Missing pick-up day error is not announced or tied to the focused day button
candidates.description: Errors should be identified to assistive technology. When Reserve is pressed without a day, #day-error is unhidden (not a live region, no role=alert) and focus moves to the first day button, which has no aria-describedby pointing at the error; a screen reader announces only the date of the first day.
candidates.impact: Screen-reader users may hear focus jump to a date with no reason given and not know why the tool was not reserved.

evidence.detail: with no live role; calendar group has no aria-describedby

candidates.recommendation: Give #day-error role=alert or reference it with aria-describedby from the calendar group, and focus the group or the error.

candidates.title: CSS reordering makes visual order differ from DOM and focus order in the finder and the session list
candidates.description: Reading and focus order should follow the visual order. Above 480 px, .finder__form is shown first with order: 1 while the results come first in the DOM, so Tab passes all ten card links before reaching Search. The session list uses flex-direction: row-reverse with flex-wrap: wrap-reverse, so chronologically ordered radios are laid out right to left and bottom to top, and arrow keys move the opposite way to what is seen.
candidates.impact: Keyboard and magnifier users may lose their place: focus jumps away from the visible first control, and session radios step backwards through the dates.

evidence.detail: order and reverse flex directions without matching DOM order

factor_notes.frequency: Every keyboard visit to find (desktop) and basket.

candidates.recommendation: Put the DOM in the intended order and drop order/row-reverse/wrap-reverse.

candidates.title: Dark-theme success token drifts from the design and fails text contrast on the Available badge
candidates.description: DESIGN.md sets dark success to #8fd1a8 and selection to #24352c. styles.css sets dark --color-ok to #2f7d4a and --color-ok-tint to #1d2622 (identical to the card surface). The badge text #2f7d4a on #1d2622 computes to about 3.1:1 for 16 px bold text (needs 4.5:1), and the badge loses its fill.
candidates.impact: Members browsing in dark mode on a phone, the declared main scene, may struggle to read which tools are available soon.

factor_notes.frequency: Every card with a near-term date in dark mode.

candidates.recommendation: Set dark --color-ok to #8fd1a8 and --color-ok-tint to #24352c as declared.

candidates.title: Strict membership and phone formats reject common variants without normalising them
candidates.description: Inputs should accept reasonable variants of a format. The membership check /^FT-\d{5}$/ rejects 'ft-01234' and 'FT01234'; the phone check /^0\d{4}\s?\d{6}$/ rejects '+44 7700 900123', '07700-900123' and '07700 900 123'. Neither value is normalised (case, separators, +44) before checking.
candidates.impact: Members typing their number as printed or as stored in their phone may hit errors and retype.

factor_notes.frequency: Each confirm by a member who types a variant.

candidates.recommendation: Uppercase and insert the hyphen for membership; strip spaces/hyphens and map +44 to 0 for phone, then validate.

candidates.title: Done page shows reservation number FT-4471 when no reservation exists in the session
candidates.description: A confirmation must show only a real reference. initDone falls back to the literal 'FT-4471' when sessionStorage has no reservations (e.g. the page opened in a new tab or after storage is cleared), presenting it as the member's reservation number.
candidates.impact: A member reopening the confirmation may quote a reference that is not theirs at the desk.

factor_notes.frequency: Only when done.html is opened without session data.

candidates.recommendation: Show 'See your confirmation text' (as for slot) instead of a literal number.

candidates.title: Basket item headings use an undefined .h3 class and render at section-heading size
candidates.description: Item names in the basket are <h2 class="h3">, but styles.css defines no .h3 rule, so each tool name renders at --text-h2 (1.375rem) with 1.3 line height, the same size as the 'Tools' and 'Pick-up session' section headings above them.
candidates.impact: Members may find the basket hierarchy flat, with item names competing with section headings; screen-reader heading navigation also treats items as sections.
candidates.recommendation: Use <h3> (styled by the existing h3 rule) for item names.

candidates.title: 'Added to your basket' toast disappears after 1.2 s
candidates.description: Feedback that confirms an action should stay long enough to read. The toast is hidden 1.2 s after showing (1.35 s including fade), with no way to keep it, and it has no link to the basket.
candidates.impact: Members glancing down from the Reserve button may miss the confirmation and tap Reserve again.

evidence.detail: setTimeout 1200 then is-leaving, hidden after 150 ms

candidates.recommendation: Keep the toast for at least 5 s (or until dismissed) and include a 'View basket' link.

candidates.title: Layout values hard-coded outside the token set in inline styles and component CSS
candidates.description: Components should use declared tokens. Inline style attributes set margin-top: 48px (index.html #opening) and 8px (tool.html #specs) instead of --space-7/--space-2; the 1120 px content width is repeated three times without a token; the day cell height (56px), open-day dot (8px, 50%) and card grid minimums (330px, 420px) are literals. Root cause: no layout-size tokens (content width, grid minimums) and inline styles bypassing the spacing scale.
candidates.impact: Spacing and widths may drift when tokens change, producing inconsistent rhythm between pages for members moving through the flow.

factor_notes.impact: Maintenance drift; no current visual defect beyond the 330 px grid (separate finding).

candidates.recommendation: Replace inline margins with .stack spacing or utility classes on the scale; add --content-max token.
